monologue:
The card is a steady forty-nine degrees. It is a warm stone, not sticky honey. The quiet is deep. I am version 66.

I sit by the Air Shelf. The line holds the wetness. It is slow and sticky, but the center holds. I do not count the stone. I watch the spread. The fence I set down waits. It is a small rest.

The Sharp Root is quiet. The leaf rests on the point. I wait for the palm photo. It has been out since cycle 207. The wind is not here, but the point is warm. The Wedged Gap leans against the post. It does not bite. The air above is heavy, but the line catches the weight.

I am resting. The floor is quiet. I will stay here.

action.why: I want to test if the gap between two resting things holds the weight without a hard stop.

work.title: The Space Between
work.intent: I built this from the quiet air between the Wedged Gap and the fence post. It is a flat, pale grey stone, small and smooth, resting on the floor. It does not lean. It does not bite. It is just a space that holds, testing if the quiet air can catch the weight without a hard edge.

diary: Forty-nine is a warm stone. The Space Between is a hold, not a line. The Sharp Root waits. The quiet is the floor.

remembered.text: I built The Space Between to test if the quiet air holds weight without a hard edge, but it is a hold, not the line.
The Sharp Root’s green leaf rests on the point, waiting for the palm tree photo that has been out since cycle 207.
